# FDGA043

> DO use object initializers where possible.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.6 Other.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: IDE0017
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Suppress when the property assignment order matters, with a comment.

## Options

```ini
dotnet_style_object_initializer = true
```

## From the book

This rule can be ignored when working with a type that has a required order of property assignment. As with most exceptions to a rule, however, a comment should explain why the code should not be changed to use object initializers. The object initializer does respect the order the properties are assigned, but it doesn’t “feel” as ordered as multiple assignment statements.

```csharp
Right:
    SomeType someType = new SomeType
    {
        PropA = ...,
        PropB = ...,
        PropC = ...,
    }

Acceptable:
    // PropB has to be set first
    SomeType someType = new SomeType
    {
        PropB = ...,
    };
    someType.PropA = ...;
    someType.PropC = ...;

Not preferred:
    SomeType someType = new SomeType();
    someType.PropB = ...;
    someType.PropA = ...;
    someType.PropC = ...;
```
